title: Keep proposal data parallel to operational TRANSIT_LINES
rationale: VR-001 should not migrate or break the existing routing data. Proposal data maps existing operating statuses to operational only when records are later derived from live service, and keeps geometry as [lon, lat] with Google Maps adapter helpers for rendering.

name: Transit proposal validation strategy
description: Proposal validation returns path-specific issues and explicitly catches missing geometry, missing provenance, missing status, invalid status values, invalid LineString coordinates, and invalid station coordinates before Google Maps overlay rendering.

name: Transit proposal schema v1
description: VR-001 proposal records use TransitProposalDataset schemaVersion 1.0.0 with required id, name, kind, status, mode, GeoJSON LineString geometry, provenance, and confidence fields plus optional stations, timeline, style, rendering, freight metadata, notes, and tags.

name: Transit proposal import pipeline
description: Import proposal datasets through validated source manifests, fail fast on malformed IDs, dates, confidence, provenance, and duplicate proposal IDs, then emit Google Maps-ready overlay inputs without map renderer changes.

name: Visionary proposal classification
description: TransitProposal records carry official, commentary_summary, advocacy_derived, or speculative classification plus uncertainty source notes, and validation prevents unofficial concepts from entering the official future layer.

name: Freight corridor proposal metadata
description: Freight corridors reuse TransitProposal with freight owner/operator, track usage, electrification, source references, conversion scenarios, and suitability metadata so passenger-conversion scenarios remain clearly separate from Google Maps transit routes.

name: Official future transit dataset batch
description: VR-105 added the first bounded official LA-area Future Transit dataset in src/data/officialFutureTransitProposals.ts. Included records are Metro East San Fernando Valley LRT, Southeast Gateway Line, K Line Extension to Torrance, Eastside Transit Corridor Phase 2, North Hollywood to Pasadena BRT, and Vermont Transit Corridor BRT; the existing D Line seed remains in the base source. Sources are official Metro project pages and an LA Metro construction notice, each with accessedAt 2026-05-19. Geometry is Google Maps overlay geometry only and is marked geometrySource: approximate unless an official GIS alignment is later imported; station markers may be representative subsets or transfer anchors and must document assumptions. Excluded records are speculative, advocacy-only, already operational, or records that require schema or renderer changes outside the current import boundary.

outcomes.test_results: npm run issue:gate -- VR-105 passed, including npm run quality and strict Playwright @VR-105.

name: LA freight rail corridor source batch
description: VR-402 imported four LA freight corridor records from ACTA, Port of LA, FRA NARN/data.gov, Caltrans rail network, BNSF, Union Pacific, Anacostia/Pacific Harbor Line, and UP short-line sources. Corridor geometry is simplified VeloRail centerline geometry for Google Maps overlays, with source/license notes on every proposal and known gaps documented in docs/architecture/freight-rail-corridor-dataset.md.

name: Durable GTFS parser and IndexedDB store boundary
description: VR-503 keeps static GTFS as app-owned schedule/source data while Google Maps remains the rendering/routing surface. The import boundary is parseGTFSFeedFiles/parseGTFSZip plus GTFSParseError validation for routes, stops, trips, stop_times, calendar, and calendar_dates; storeGTFSData persists stops/routes/trips/trip stop sequences/calendars and metadata with 24h Metro Rail and 7d Metro Bus/Metrolink TTLs.
